issue.title: Add MIP-06: Group Voice and Video Calling
issue.body:
Specifies privacy-preserving real-time voice and video calling within Marmot groups. Media is E2EE using SFrame with keys derived from MLS epoch exporter secret. Call signaling travels as MLS app messages. Tiered media topology scales from p2p mesh to cascaded SFU federation. New event kinds 450-454 (call signaling), 10052 (SFU advertisement). Depends on MIPs 00, 01, 03, 05. Includes test vectors and wire format constants.

+# MIP-06
+
+## Multi-Device Support
+
+`draft` `optional`
+
+This document defines how users can operate Marmot on multiple devices simultaneously. Each device is an independent MLS leaf node that joins existing groups via External Commits, authorized through an out-of-band device pairing flow. This specification covers the authorization model, pairing protocol, payload format, and client recommendations for multi-device scenarios.
+
+## Overview
+
+Marmot's identity model naturally supports multiple devices. Each device generates its own MLS signing key and encryption key, but all devices belonging to the same user share the same Nostr public key in their MLS `BasicCredential` identity field (see [MIP-00](00.md)). This means a user with two devices in a group will occupy two separate leaf nodes in the ratchet tree, but both leaf nodes carry the same credential identity.
+
+The multi-device model has these properties:
+
+- **Independent state**: Each device maintains its own MLS group state, key material, and message history. There is no shared MLS state between devices.
+- **Same logical identity**: All devices share the same Nostr pubkey, allowing clients to recognize multiple leaf nodes as belonging to one user.
+- **Independent decryption**: Each device independently receives and decrypts group messages. A message sent from one device will appear on the user's other devices as a group message.
+- **Forward secrecy boundary**: A new device cannot decrypt messages from epochs before it joined. This is a fundamental MLS property and is by design.
+
+History synchronization between devices is out of scope for this MIP and is deferred to a future specification.
+
+## Multi-Device Signaling (CRITICAL)
+
+To prevent state divergence between clients that do and do not implement this MIP, multi-device External Commit behavior MUST be explicitly signaled at the MLS group level.
+
+### Extension Identifier
+
+This extension uses identifier `0xF2F0`.
+
+```tls
+struct {
+    uint16 version;  // current: 1
+} MarmotMultiDevice;
+```
+
+Version rules:
+
+- Version `0` is reserved and MUST be rejected.
+- Version `1` is the current format.
+- Higher versions MUST be rejected unless explicitly supported.

issue.title: feat(MIP-06): Multi-Device Support
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds MIP-06: Multi-Device Support, plus the cross-MIP clarifications needed to make it operationally consistent with the current Marmot spec set.

This defines how one Nostr identity can participate in the same MLS group from multiple devices, where each device is an independent leaf that joins via External Commits.

Closes #43

## Files Updated

- `06.md` — full MIP-06 specification
- `01.md` — clarified Marmot's TLS-notation + QUIC-varint wire-format convention
- `03.md` — MIP-06 commit exception, leaf-scoped SelfRemove guidance, and `authenticated_data` rules
- `threat_model.md` — expanded multi-device-specific threats and validation requirements
- `README.md` — MIP table entry

## Current Design

- **Join mechanism**: MLS External Commits (RFC 9420 §12.4.3.2)
- **Group gating**: MIP-06 is enabled only when `marmot_multi_device` (`0xF2F0`) is present in `GroupContext.extensions`, required in `required_capabilities`, and advertised in member capabilities
- **Existing-group migration**: current leaves update capabilities first; only then can admins enable `0xF2F0` at the group level
- **Authorization checks**:
  - joining credential identity matches an existing member identity
  - valid Nostr identity proof in `FramedContent.authenticated_data`
  - exactly one Resumption PSK proposal (`usage = application`)
  - no `Remove` proposals (join-style External Commits only)
  - normal MLS / LeafNode validation
- **Identity proof**: canonical unsigned Nostr proof event (`kind: 450`) signed using standard Nostr event signing and carried in `authenticated_data`; the proof event MUST NOT be published to relays
- **Outer encryption**: `group_event_key = MLS-Exporter("marmot", "group-event", 32)`; pairing payload transfers the exact current-epoch `group_event_key` plus `resumption_psk` and `GroupInfo`
- **Pairing transport**: X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + ChaCha20-Poly1305; Phase 1 bootstrap must use an authenticated channel or explicit key verification
- **Retry model**: incremental refresh uses the original new-device recipient key plus a fresh existing-device ephemeral keypair for each refresh message
- **Optional device metadata**: encrypted device-name extension (`0xF2EF`)
- **Admin model**: admin status remains identity-based, so new leaves for an admin identity inherit admin privileges immediately

## Additional Spec Tightening Included

- Uses Marmot's established TLS-notation / QUIC-varint serialization convention consistently with MIP-01
- Simplifies pairing-payload versioning to a single outer payload version
- Expands the payload `groups` vector to `2^32-1` bytes to support large multi-group sessions
- Makes non-MIP-06 Commit `authenticated_data` empty by default unless another Marmot spec defines otherwise
- Clarifies that SelfRemove is leaf-scoped in multi-device groups
- Adds client guidance to surface device additions, especially for admin identities and suspicious repeated same-identity joins
- Adds threat-model coverage for:
  - External Commit flooding / epoch-churn DoS
  - Phase-1 bootstrap key substitution / MITM

## Out of Scope / Deferred

- History synchronization between devices
- Mandatory stable cross-group device identifier / guaranteed “remove this device from every group” semantics

Another day another problem, but this time I come bearing gifts in the form of minor spec changes **TL;DR:** The identity proof challenge hashes `serialized_LeafNode`, but the LeafNode's HPKE key isn't generated until after `authenticated_data` must be set. Changing the challenge to hash `credential_identity || signature_key` instead fixes this. Both are known upfront, and it's a tighter binding anyway. --- AI generated and human cleaned description: ## The Problem ### 1. What the Challenge Hash Currently Binds To The spec defines: ``` challenge = SHA-256("marmot-external-commit-v1" || serialized_LeafNode || serialized_GroupContext) ``` A TLS-serialized `LeafNode` contains six fields: | Field | Identity-relevant? | Known before External Commit is built? | |---|---|---| | `credential` (Nostr pubkey) | **Yes** | **Yes**, duh | | `signature_key` (MLS signing pubkey) | **Yes** | **Yes** | | `capabilities` | No | Yes | | `extensions` | No | Yes | | `encryption_key` (HPKE pubkey) | No | **No**, generated by `compute_path()` inside `build()` | | `leaf_node_source` (parent hash) | No | **No**, computed from ratchet tree diff inside `build()` | The last two fields are generated deep inside OpenMLS during commit construction. Because the challenge includes the full serialized LeafNode, it cannot be computed until after `build()`, but `authenticated_data` must be set before `build_group()`, which runs earlier. ### 2. The Ordering Constraint ```mermaid graph LR A["with_aad(proof)
AAD must be set HERE"] --> B["build_group()
captures AAD in ExternalCommitInfo"] B --> C["add_psk_proposal()
load_psks()"] C --> D["build()
compute_path() creates LeafNode
❌ too late to change AAD"] style A fill:#2d6a4f,stroke:#1b4332,color:#fff style B fill:#e9c46a,stroke:#e76f51,color:#1b4332 style C fill:#e9c46a,stroke:#e76f51,color:#1b4332 style D fill:#e76f51,stroke:#c1440e,color:#fff ``` `ExternalCommitBuilder::with_aad()` must be called before `build_group()` (captured at `external_commits.rs:309`), but `compute_path()` generates the HPKE key and parent hash inside `build()` (`commit_builder.rs:606`). There is no public API to set AAD between these two points. ### 3. Why We Don't Need the Full LeafNode The identity proof's purpose is to prove the Nostr private key holder authorized **this device's signing key** to join **this group at this epoch**. The HPKE encryption key and parent hash are: - **Identity-irrelevant**; they're ephemeral tree-key material, not identity material - **Already bound** by MLS itself; `confirmation_tag` validation and the tree hash in `GroupContext` cover these fields They create a circular dependency with the AAD ordering; the narrower binding is stronger: it targets exactly the identity-relevant fields. ### 4. The Fix Change the challenge to: ``` challenge = SHA-256("marmot-external-commit-v1" || credential_identity || signature_key || serialized_GroupContext) ``` Where: - `credential_identity` = raw Nostr pubkey bytes from the `BasicCredential` (32 bytes) - `signature_key` = MLS signature public key bytes from the `CredentialWithKey` Both are supplied by the application before `build_group()` is called. On the verification side, both are extracted from the joining LeafNode in the staged commit. I've already implemented and tested this in the SDK. The full External Commit flow with identity proof construction, AAD, and cryptographic verification works end-to-end with no upstream OpenMLS changes. ### 5. Spec Lines to Update **Proof Construction** (§Proof Construction, steps 1 and 3): ```diff -1. Serialize the LeafNode from the External Commit's UpdatePath using TLS serialization. +1. Extract `credential_identity` (raw Nostr pubkey bytes from the BasicCredential) + and `signature_key` (MLS signature public key bytes) from the `CredentialWithKey` + used to construct the External Commit. Both are known before the commit is built. -3. Compute the challenge: `challenge = SHA-256(ASCII("marmot-external-commit-v1") || serialized_LeafNode || serialized_GroupContext)`. +3. Compute the challenge: `challenge = SHA-256(ASCII("marmot-external-commit-v1") || credential_identity || signature_key || serialized_GroupContext)`. ``` **Proof Verification** (§Proof Verification, steps 3 and 5): ```diff -3. Serialize the LeafNode from the External Commit's UpdatePath. +3. Extract `credential_identity` (raw credential identity bytes) and `signature_key` + (signature public key bytes) from the LeafNode in the External Commit's UpdatePath. -5. Compute `challenge = SHA-256(ASCII("marmot-external-commit-v1") || serialized_LeafNode || serialized_GroupContext)`. +5. Compute `challenge = SHA-256(ASCII("marmot-external-commit-v1") || credential_identity || signature_key || serialized_GroupContext)`. ``` **Security Properties** (§Security Properties, "Identity binding"): ```diff -- **Identity binding**: Proves the Nostr private key holder authorized this specific LeafNode to join this specific group at this specific epoch. +- **Identity binding**: Proves the Nostr private key holder authorized this specific credential and signing key to join this specific group at this specific epoch. ``` **Replay Protection** (§Replay Protection): ```diff -Nostr identity proof further binds to specific LeafNode + GroupContext. +Nostr identity proof further binds to specific credential identity, signature key, and GroupContext. ```

+# MIP-06
+
+## Multi-Device Support
+
+`draft` `optional`
+
+This document defines how users can operate Marmot on multiple devices simultaneously. Each device is an independent MLS leaf node that joins existing groups via External Commits, authorized through an out-of-band device pairing flow. This specification covers the authorization model, pairing protocol, payload format, and client recommendations for multi-device scenarios.
+
+## Overview
+
+Marmot's identity model naturally supports multiple devices. Each device generates its own MLS signing key and encryption key, but all devices belonging to the same user share the same Nostr public key in their MLS `BasicCredential` identity field (see [MIP-00](00.md)). This means a user with two devices in a group will occupy two separate leaf nodes in the ratchet tree, but both leaf nodes carry the same credential identity.
+
+The multi-device model has these properties:
+
+- **Independent state**: Each device maintains its own MLS group state, key material, and message history. There is no shared MLS state between devices.
+- **Same logical identity**: All devices share the same Nostr pubkey, allowing clients to recognize multiple leaf nodes as belonging to one user.
+- **Independent decryption**: Each device independently receives and decrypts group messages. A message sent from one device will appear on the user's other devices as a group message.
+- **Forward secrecy boundary**: A new device cannot decrypt messages from epochs before it joined. This is a fundamental MLS property and is by design.
+
+History synchronization between devices is out of scope for this MIP and is deferred to a future specification.

## Summary

Expands the encrypted token size specification in MIP-05 from 280 bytes to 1084 bytes to accommodate larger device tokens and improve padding uniformity.

## Changes

- **Token size**: Updated `EncryptedToken` from 280 to 1084 bytes
  - Ephemeral pubkey: 32 bytes
  - Nonce: 12 bytes
  - Ciphertext: 1040 bytes (increased from 236)

- **Plaintext payload**: Updated `TokenPlaintext` from 220 to 1024 bytes
  - Platform: 1 byte
  - Token length: 2 bytes
  - Device token: up to 1021 bytes
  - Random padding: fills remaining space

- **Validation**: Updated token_length constraints to 1-1021 bytes (from platform-specific 1-200 for FCM, 32 for APNs)

- **Batching recommendations**: Reduced from 100 tokens per event to 25 tokens per event (due to larger token size)

- **Updated all examples and documentation** to reflect new size constraints throughout the specification

The following is a manually cleaned up AI-generated summary. I'm pretty confident it's correct, but it *is* AI, so... grain of salt. **TL;DR:** A new device joining via external commit cannot look up the resumption PSK because `ResumptionPskStore` starts empty and OpenMLS exposes no way to pre-populate it. --- ## The Problem ### 1. Normal Path (Existing Member Commits) When an existing group member creates a commit with a PSK proposal, the group already has state, including a populated `resumption_psk_store`: ```mermaid graph LR A["MlsGroup
has group state"] --> B["group_epoch_secrets"] B --> C["ResumptionPskStore"] C --> D["Vec‹GroupEpoch, ResumptionPskSecret›
populated by MLS key schedule"] style A fill:#2d6a4f,stroke:#1b4332,color:#fff style B fill:#40916c,stroke:#2d6a4f,color:#fff style C fill:#52b788,stroke:#40916c,color:#fff style D fill:#95d5b2,stroke:#52b788,color:#1b4332 ``` Commit creation follows this chain: ```rust commit_builder .add_psk_proposal(psk) .load_psks(storage) .build(...) .finalize(...) ``` `load_psks()` at `commit_builder.rs:336` resolves through `psk.rs:520–535`: ```rust match &psk_id.psk { Psk::Resumption(resumption) => { if let Some(psk_bundle) = resumption_psk_store.get(resumption.psk_epoch()) { psk_bundles.push((psk_id, psk_bundle.secret.clone())); // ✅ found } else { return Err(PskError::KeyNotFound); } } // ... ``` The store is a ring buffer populated epoch-by-epoch as the group evolves, so lookups always succeed for existing members. --- ### 2. External Commit Path (New Device Joining) When a new device calls `ExternalCommitBuilder::build_group()`, the group is constructed from scratch: ```rust // line 290 let mut mls_group = MlsGroup { // ... resumption_psk_store: ResumptionPskStore::new(32), // ⚠️ empty // ... }; ``` The new device has no epoch history. The store starts empty. Then the commit flow runs: ```rust commit_builder .add_psk_proposal(resumption_psk_proposal) // required by MIP-06 .load_psks(provider.storage()) // ❌ searches empty store → KeyNotFound ``` ```mermaid graph LR A["New Device
ExternalCommitBuilder"] --> B["build_group()
ResumptionPskStore::new(32)"] B --> C["load_psks()
searches empty store"] C --> D["PskError::KeyNotFound"] style A fill:#264653,stroke:#1d3557,color:#fff style B fill:#e76f51,stroke:#c1440e,color:#fff style C fill:#e76f51,stroke:#c1440e,color:#fff style D fill:#9b2226,stroke:#641220,color:#fff ``` --- ### 3. Why the Existing Device Can't Help The existing device **does** know the resumption PSK (it's in the pairing payload), but there is no mechanism to inject it into the new device's store: | # | Barrier | Detail | |---|---------|--------| | 1 | `ResumptionPskStore` is `pub(crate)` | Cannot be constructed outside `openmls` | | 2 | `ResumptionPskStore::add()` is `pub(crate)` | Cannot insert entries externally | | 3 | No `MlsGroup` injection method | No public API to add a PSK to the store | | 4 | Store is not in `StorageProvider` | In-memory struct owned by `MlsGroup`, no storage workaround | --- ### 4. What Would Fix It OpenMLS needs to expose one of: | Option | API | Tradeoff | |--------|-----|----------| | A | `MlsGroup::inject_resumption_psk(epoch, secret)` | Simple but exposes internal store mutation | | B | Public `ResumptionPskStore` constructor + setter on `MlsGroup` | Flexible but leaks implementation details | | **C** | **`ExternalCommitBuilder::with_resumption_psk(epoch, secret)`** | **Cleanest: keeps store private, scoped to external commit path** | **Recommended: Option C.** It keeps the internal store private while allowing the external commit path to supply PSK material received out-of-band.

+# MIP-06
+
+## Multi-Device Support
+
+`draft` `optional`
+
+This document defines how users can operate Marmot on multiple devices simultaneously. Each device is an independent MLS leaf node that joins existing groups via External Commits, authorized through an out-of-band device pairing flow. This specification covers the authorization model, pairing protocol, payload format, and client recommendations for multi-device scenarios.
+
+## Overview
+
+Marmot's identity model naturally supports multiple devices. Each device generates its own MLS signing key and encryption key, but all devices belonging to the same user share the same Nostr public key in their MLS `BasicCredential` identity field (see [MIP-00](00.md)). This means a user with two devices in a group will occupy two separate leaf nodes in the ratchet tree, but both leaf nodes carry the same credential identity.
+
+The multi-device model has these properties:
+
+- **Independent state**: Each device maintains its own MLS group state, key material, and message history. There is no shared MLS state between devices.
+- **Same logical identity**: All devices share the same Nostr pubkey, allowing clients to recognize multiple leaf nodes as belonging to one user.
+- **Independent decryption**: Each device independently receives and decrypts group messages. A message sent from one device will appear on the user's other devices as a group message.
+- **Forward secrecy boundary**: A new device cannot decrypt messages from epochs before it joined. This is a fundamental MLS property and is by design.
+
+History synchronization between devices is out of scope for this MIP and is deferred to a future specification.
+
+## Multi-Device Signaling (CRITICAL)
+
+To prevent state divergence between clients that do and do not implement this MIP, multi-device External Commit behavior MUST be explicitly signaled at the MLS group level.
+
+### Extension Identifier
+
+This extension uses identifier `0xF2F0`.
+
+```tls
+struct {
+    uint16 version;  // current: 1
+} MarmotMultiDevice;
+```
+
+Version rules:
+
+- Version `0` is reserved and MUST be rejected.
+- Version `1` is the current format.
+- Higher versions MUST be rejected unless explicitly supported.
+
+### Signaling Rules
+
+A group that enables MIP-06 External Commit behavior MUST satisfy all of the following:
+
+1. Include the `0xF2F0` `marmot_multi_device` extension in `GroupContext.extensions`.
+2. Include `0xF2F0` in the group's `required_capabilities` extension list.
+3. Ensure each member's `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions` includes `0xF2F0` (standard MLS compatibility rule).
+
+### Compatibility Behavior
+
+- If any part of the MIP-06 signaling gate is missing, clients MUST treat External Commits from `new_member_commit` senders as unauthorized and reject them. The signaling gate requires all of the following: `GroupContext.extensions` contains a valid `marmot_multi_device` (`0xF2F0`) extension, `GroupContext.required_capabilities` requires `0xF2F0`, and at least one existing member advertises `0xF2F0` in its `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`.
+- Only if all three signaling conditions are met MAY clients apply the External Commit authorization rules in this MIP.
+
+This design lets groups decide at creation time (or through an explicit GroupContextExtensions update) whether MIP-06 behavior is enabled. The rollout requirement above is intentionally stricter than the runtime acceptance gate: admins MUST wait until every current leaf advertises `0xF2F0` before enabling MIP-06, while implementations validating an External Commit also require at least one existing member advertisement as an explicit cross-check against malformed, stale, or downgraded group state.
+
+### Enabling MIP-06 in Existing Groups
+
+Existing groups can enable MIP-06 later, but the rollout MUST be staged carefully:
+
+1. Each current member that implements MIP-06 SHOULD update its current LeafNode capabilities to advertise `0xF2F0` in `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`, typically via a regular self-update Commit.
+2. Clients that implement MIP-06 SHOULD also re-publish future KeyPackages advertising `0xF2F0` so future group additions see consistent capability signaling.
+3. Admins MUST NOT add `marmot_multi_device` to `GroupContext.extensions` or add `0xF2F0` to `required_capabilities` until every current leaf in the ratchet tree advertises `0xF2F0` in `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`.
+4. Once all current leaves advertise `0xF2F0` in `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`, an admin MAY commit a `GroupContextExtensions` update that enables `marmot_multi_device` and requires `0xF2F0` at the group level.
+5. If any current member cannot update its LeafNode capabilities, the group MUST NOT enable MIP-06 until that member is removed or migrated.
+
+## External Commit Authorization
+
+Devices join existing groups via MLS External Commits ([RFC 9420 Section 12.4.3.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.html#section-12.4.3.2)). An External Commit allows a new party to add themselves to a group using a `GroupInfo` object, without requiring an existing member to come online and issue an Add proposal.
+
+### Authorization Carve-Out
+
+[MIP-03](03.md) requires that Commits other than self-update Commits and SelfRemove-only Commits be sent by a member listed in `admin_pubkeys`. External Commits from new devices use a carve-out only when MIP-06 signaling is enabled (see [Multi-Device Signaling](#multi-device-signaling-critical)).
+
+**An External Commit MUST be accepted when ALL of the following conditions are met:**
+
+1. `GroupContext.extensions` contains a valid `marmot_multi_device` (`0xF2F0`) extension
+2. `GroupContext.required_capabilities` requires `0xF2F0`
+3. At least one existing group member advertises `0xF2F0` in `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`
+4. The credential identity (Nostr pubkey) in the joining LeafNode matches the credential identity of at least one existing group member
+5. The External Commit includes exactly one valid Resumption PSK proposal (see [Resumption PSK Requirement](#resumption-psk-requirement))
+6. The External Commit includes a valid Nostr identity proof in `FramedContent.authenticated_data` (see [Nostr Identity Proof](#nostr-identity-proof))
+7. The External Commit contains no `Remove` proposals. MIP-06 permits only join-style External Commits, not resync-style External Commits that replace an existing leaf.
+8. The External Commit satisfies all standard MLS validation rules ([RFC 9420 Section 12.4.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.html#section-12.4.2))
+
+**An External Commit MUST be rejected when:**
+
+- `GroupContext.extensions` does not contain a valid `marmot_multi_device` (`0xF2F0`) extension
+- `GroupContext.required_capabilities` does not require `0xF2F0`
+- No existing group member advertises `0xF2F0` in `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`
+- The credential identity does not match any existing member's credential identity
+- The Resumption PSK proposal is missing or invalid
+- The Nostr identity proof is missing or fails verification
+- The External Commit includes any `Remove` proposal
+- Any standard MLS validation check fails
+
+This carve-out ensures that only the holder of a Nostr private key that is already represented in the group can add a new device, and only in groups that explicitly enabled this behavior.
+
+### Validation Steps
+
+When processing an External Commit, existing members MUST perform these checks in order:
+
+1. Decrypt the outer group-event encryption layer using the current epoch's `group_event_key` (standard `kind: 445` processing per [MIP-03](03.md)).
+2. Verify the MLS `PublicMessage` structure and signature per [RFC 9420](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.html).
+3. Verify `GroupContext.extensions` contains a valid `marmot_multi_device` (`0xF2F0`) extension.
+4. Verify `GroupContext.required_capabilities` requires `0xF2F0`.
+5. Verify at least one existing group member advertises `0xF2F0` in `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`.
+6. Validate the joining LeafNode per [RFC 9420 Section 7.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.html#section-7.3) before using any fields from it.
+7. Verify the credential identity in the joining LeafNode matches an existing member's credential identity.
+8. Verify `authenticated_data` contains a valid Nostr identity proof (see [Nostr Identity Proof](#nostr-identity-proof)).
+9. Verify exactly one `PreSharedKey` proposal is present and that:
+   - `psktype == resumption`
+   - `usage == application`
+   - `psk_group_id == FramedContent.group_id`
+   - `psk_epoch == FramedContent.epoch` (the current group epoch for this Commit)
+   - `psk_nonce` length equals `KDF.Nh`
+10. Verify the External Commit contains no `Remove` proposals.

An External Commit allows a new party to add themselves to a group using a `GroupInfo` object, without requiring an existing member to come online and issue an Add proposal.
+
+### Authorization Carve-Out
+
+[MIP-03](03.md) requires that Commits other than self-update Commits and SelfRemove-only Commits be sent by a member listed in `admin_pubkeys`. External Commits from new devices use a carve-out only when MIP-06 signaling is enabled (see [Multi-Device Signaling](#multi-device-signaling-critical)).
+
+**An External Commit MUST be accepted when ALL of the following conditions are met:**
+
+1. `GroupContext.extensions` contains a valid `marmot_multi_device` (`0xF2F0`) extension
+2. `GroupContext.required_capabilities` requires `0xF2F0`
+3. At least one existing group member advertises `0xF2F0` in `LeafNode.capabilities.extensions`
